related.why: Reading the distal radius X-ray and planning treatment
Scaphoid injury after a fall on the outstretched hand

brief.setting: Emergency department plaster room, with a volunteer or manikin arm
brief.role: Core surgical trainee on call for orthopaedics
brief.scenario: Mr Rhys Maddock, 38, fell on his outstretched right hand. X-rays show an undisplaced extra-articular distal radius fracture. The orthopaedic plan is a below-elbow backslab and fracture clinic. Plaster of Paris, undercast padding, crepe bandage, water and scissors are provided.
brief.task: Apply a below-elbow backslab, talking the examiner through each step, and give aftercare advice.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Check the plan, examine the hand, position, pad, measure, apply, mould, recheck, advise.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Forgetting to recheck the circulation and nerves once the slab is on.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "I'll confirm his details, the side and the X-ray, and examine his hand before I start."

grid.label: Prepare and consent
grid.fail: Starts without checking the X-ray, side or plan, or without explaining.
grid.pass: Confirms identity, side, X-ray and orthopaedic plan; explains the backslab; gains consent; gives analgesia; removes rings and watch.
grid.high: Asks about diabetes, skin conditions and allergies; explains a backslab leaves room for swelling.

grid.label: Neurovascular check before
grid.fail: Doesn't examine skin, circulation or nerves before applying.
grid.pass: Documents skin integrity, radial pulse, capillary refill, and median, ulnar and radial nerve sensation and movement.
grid.high: Tests the median nerve carefully (index pulp, thumb abduction), as distal radius fractures can cause acute carpal tunnel syndrome.

grid.label: Position and padding
grid.fail: Applies plaster without padding, or with the wrist forced into flexion.
grid.pass: Positions the wrist in neutral before padding; applies undercast padding smoothly and evenly, with extra over the ulnar styloid.
grid.high: Keeps the limb supported in position until set, because movement causes ridges and pressure sores.

grid.label: Measure and wet
grid.fail: Makes the slab so long it blocks the knuckles or the elbow.
grid.pass: Measures dorsally from the metacarpal heads to just below the elbow; soaks in lukewarm water; squeezes gently.
grid.high: Knows water at about 20–25°C: hot water speeds setting and can burn; trims to free the MCP joints and thumb.

grid.label: Apply and mould
grid.fail: Bandages tightly, or moulds with the fingertips.
grid.pass: Lays the slab dorsally over the padding, secures with a bandage without tension, moulds with the palms.
grid.high: Smooths the edges, rests the arm on a pillow while it sets, and checks full finger flexion and thumb opposition.

grid.label: Recheck (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Doesn't recheck circulation and nerves after application.
grid.pass: Rechecks and documents circulation, sensation and movement after application.
grid.high: Knows pain out of proportion or on passive finger stretch suggests compartment syndrome: release bandages to skin, elevate, reassess within 30 minutes.

grid.label: Aftercare
grid.fail: Sends him home without cast care or warning advice.
grid.pass: Verbal and written advice: elevate, move fingers, keep dry, analgesia; return if worsening pain, numbness or discolouration; consultant review in 24 h, plan 72 h.
grid.high: Gives a 24-hour contact number; checks he understands when to return; advises not to push anything down the plaster.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Starts wetting plaster without checking the X-ray or the side.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Applies wet plaster directly to the skin with the wrist flexed.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Cuts a slab running from the fingertips to above the elbow.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Wraps the crepe bandage tightly; presses dents in with the fingertips.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Mr Maddock, can I confirm your date of birth? It's your right wrist, and this X-ray is yours. I'm going to put a plaster splint on the back of your forearm. Is that OK? Have you had painkillers? Can we take your rings and watch off?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Checks the skin, radial pulse and capillary refill, and sensation and movement for the median, ulnar and radial nerves; documents them.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Positions the wrist in neutral, then applies padding smoothly with extra over the ulnar styloid.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Measures on the back of the forearm from the knuckles to just below the elbow; soaks the plaster in lukewarm water and squeezes gently.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Lays the slab on the back of the forearm, secures it with the bandage without tension, and moulds with the palms.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Rechecks and documents circulation, sensation and movement.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Keep your arm raised, move your fingers, keep the plaster dry and take painkillers. Come back straight away if the pain gets worse, or your fingers go numb, swollen or discoloured. Here is a leaflet. A named fracture consultant will review your case within 24 hours, in person or in a virtual trauma meeting, and you'll have a definitive plan within 72 hours.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Any diabetes, skin problems or allergies? This slab covers the back of the arm only, so it leaves room for swelling.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Tests index pulp sensation and thumb abduction.] Distal radius fractures can compress the median nerve, so I want a clear baseline.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Asks an assistant to support the arm in neutral until the plaster has set.] Movement while it sets makes ridges that cause sores.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Checks the water.] Lukewarm, about 20 to 25 degrees: hot water sets it faster and can burn. [Trims the slab so the knuckles and thumb move freely.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Smooths the edges, rests the arm on a pillow.] Make a fist for me, and touch your thumb to your little finger. Good.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Rechecks.] If pain became severe, or hurt when I straightened his fingers, I'd loosen everything to the skin, elevate, reassess within 30 minutes and call my senior.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Here's the number to ring, day or night. Can you tell me what would make you come back? And please don't push anything down the plaster to scratch.

failures.move: Not rechecking circulation and nerves after application.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: a tight slab or developing compartment syndrome is missed.
Cannot tell whether a later deficit came from the injury or the plaster.

failures.move: No padding, or wrist forced into flexion.
failures.consequence: Pressure sores, median nerve compression and stiffness.
He doesn't know to return with worsening pain or numbness.

recovery.when: You forget to check the hand first
recovery.line: Before I go further, I'll document his circulation and nerves.

recovery.when: He complains the slab feels tight
recovery.line: I'll loosen the bandage, elevate and recheck his hand now.

knowledge.fact: Assess and record neurovascular status before and after casting; give verbal and written advice including when to return.
Position the limb before padding; pad bony prominences; mould with palms; lukewarm water about 20–25°C.
Distal radius: wrist neutral, not forced palmar flexion.
Fracture pathway: named consultant review within 24 h (in person or virtual); definitive plan within 72 h.
Suspected compartment syndrome: release circumferential dressings to skin, elevate, reassess within 30 minutes.
Children's buckle (torus) fractures: no rigid cast.

recall.think: Compartment syndrome, median nerve compression, pressure sores.
recall.say: "I'll check his hand before and after the slab."
do: Pad, position neutral, dorsal slab to below elbow

numbers.meaning: reassess after releasing dressings for suspected compartment syndrome

recall.trap: Assuming a backslab can't be too tight.
recall.finish: Neurovascular status documented, written advice, fracture clinic booked.

sources.name: British Orthopaedic Association Casting Committee. Casting Standards
sources.supports: Explain and gain consent; ask about diabetes, skin and allergies; assess and record neurovascular status before and after; position the limb before padding and maintain until set; pad bony prominences such as the ulnar styloid; plaster of Paris for fresh fractures; lukewarm water usually 20–25°C, hot water speeds setting and can burn; mould with palms not fingers; rest on a pillow; trim to allow movement of joints not in the cast; verbal and written instructions, emergency contact numbers covering 24 hours, when to return

sources.name: British Orthopaedic Association. BOAST: The management of distal radial fractures
sources.supports: Document skin, circulation and sensation at presentation; wrist in neutral, not forced palmar flexion; information on recovery and rehabilitation

sources.name: British Orthopaedic Association. BOASt: Outpatient and on-call services for people with fractures or musculoskeletal injury
sources.supports: Named consultant review of the case within 24 hours of first presentation, in person or virtually in a trauma meeting, outcome sent to patient and GP; definitive treatment plan documented within 72 hours of first presentation; system to signpost patients to orthopaedic advice for concerns

sources.name: British Orthopaedic Association. BOAST: Diagnosis and management of compartment syndrome of the extremities
sources.supports: Pain out of proportion and pain on passive movement; release circumferential dressings to expose the skin, elevate, re-evaluate within 30 minutes; senior review

sources.name: NICE NG38. Fractures (non-complex): assessment and management
sources.supports: Do not use a rigid cast for torus fractures of the distal radius (1.3.3); discharge children with torus fractures after first assessment (1.3.4); verbal and written information for patients with fractures (1.6)

sources.name: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery (O'Connell, McCaskie, Sayers, eds)
sources.supports: Complications of plaster casts; carpal tunnel compression after distal radius fracture

sources.name: ICBSE Guide to the intercollegiate MRCS examination
sources.supports: Station format: 9 minutes with 1 minute's reading; examiner-led questioning in applied knowledge stations

partner.opening: Please apply a below-elbow backslab to Mr Maddock's right arm, talking me through it.

reveals.trigger: Candidate examines the hand before applying
reveals.finding: Skin intact. Radial pulse present, capillary refill 2 seconds. Sensation and movement normal in all three nerve territories.
Right-handed joiner. No diabetes or skin problems. No allergies. Paracetamol and codeine given 30 minutes ago.
Fingers pink, capillary refill 2 seconds, sensation normal, full finger flexion.

push.question: What position is the wrist in, and why?
push.expect: Neutral; forced flexion risks median nerve compression and stiffness.

push.question: How long is the slab?
push.expect: Metacarpal heads to just below the elbow, leaving MCP joints and thumb free.

push.question: What would make you worried afterwards?
push.expect: Pain out of proportion, pain on passive stretch, numbness, poor perfusion.

curveballs.prompt: An hour later he says his fingers are tingling and the pain is much worse.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Release all bandages and padding to skin, elevate, reassess within 30 minutes; senior review for possible compartment syndrome.

curveballs.prompt: The next patient is an 8-year-old with a buckle fracture of the distal radius.
curveballs.safeAnswer: No rigid cast or backslab. Discharge after first assessment; further review isn't usually needed.

curveballs.prompt: The water is hot from the tap.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Use lukewarm water: hot water speeds setting and can burn his skin.
